name: Honey BBQ Chicken Mac and Cheese

prose.intro_html:
Honey BBQ chicken mac and cheese sounds like a cheat meal, and that is exactly why it is worth doing right. Most versions load you up on cream and butter and leave you hungry an hour later. This one flips the math. We blend cottage cheese and light cream cheese into the sauce so the creamy part carries protein instead of just fat, then we crown every bowl with air fried chicken tossed in honey and BBQ sauce.

The result is a bowl that reads like comfort food and performs like a training meal: {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving. You get the sticky, sweet, smoky chicken up top and a smooth cheese sauce underneath, and you get fourteen of those bowls out of one afternoon in the kitchen. That is the whole idea around here. Eat food you actually look forward to, and pay a fair price for it.
prose.shop_smart:
This is a two-part shop: the sauce and the chicken. Handle them like two lists and it goes fast.

  • Buy the family pack of boneless skinless chicken breast. You need three pounds, and the big pack is how meal prep is supposed to be bought. Dice it at home rather than paying for pre-cut.
  • For the sauce, grab a tub of fat free cottage cheese, a block or two of light cream cheese, and a bag of reduced fat shredded cheddar. Shredded is fine here since it all goes in the blender anyway, so do not overthink block versus bag.
  • The pantry spices, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, black pepper, and dried parsley, are ones you likely already own. Check the rack before you add them to the cart so you are not buying a second jar of paprika.
  • Honey, yellow mustard, and a bottle of BBQ sauce round it out. Any BBQ sauce you like the taste of works, since we lean on the honey for the sticky glaze.
  • Buy a two-plus pound box of dry pasta. A short shape like ziti or elbow macaroni holds the sauce best.
prose.make_it:
Start with the chicken. Toss the diced chicken breast with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper until every piece is coated. If you are using the air fryer, preheat it to 350F, mist the chicken with cooking spray, and cook 10 to 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until golden and cooked through. No air fryer? Heat a nonstick pan over medium, spray it, and cook the seasoned chicken 6 to 8 minutes until browned and done.

Now the good part. Move the hot chicken to a bowl and toss it with the honey and BBQ sauce until it is glossy all over, then return it to the heat for another minute or two so the glaze caramelizes and grips the chicken. Set it aside.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta to the package directions. Before you drain, dip out about a quarter cup of the pasta water and keep it, then drain the pasta and set it aside. That starchy water is your safety net for the sauce.

For the sauce, load the blender with the cottage cheese, light cream cheese, shredded cheddar, milk, garlic powder, parsley, black pepper, paprika, salt, and mustard. Blend until it is completely smooth. Pour it into a saucepan and warm it over medium-low, stirring now and then, for 3 to 5 minutes until it thickens and turns glossy. If it stiffens up, loosen it with a splash of that reserved pasta water.

Fold the drained pasta into the sauce and stir until every noodle is coated, adding more pasta water a little at a time until it looks creamy, not gluey. Let the mac and cheese rest for 10 minutes so the flavors settle and the sauce tightens. Spoon it into bowls, pile the honey BBQ chicken on top, and finish with a pinch of parsley.
prose.portion_html:
This batch makes fourteen servings, and the honest way to split it evenly is to weigh it, not eyeball it. Keep the mac and the chicken separate for portioning. Set your empty pot on the scale and zero it out, then pour the finished mac and cheese back in and read the total weight. Divide that number by fourteen and that is your grams of pasta per container.

Do the same with the honey BBQ chicken in its bowl: total weight divided by fourteen is the chicken that goes on top of each one. Spoon the mac into fourteen containers, crown each with its share of chicken, and you have fourteen identical {{cal}} calorie, {{protein}} gram protein bowls. No guessing, no one container coming up short on payday.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is where it earns its place in the rotation. All in, this comes to ${{cost_ps}} per serving for a bowl carrying {{protein}} grams of protein. Try ordering honey BBQ chicken mac anywhere and see what it runs you, then look at that number again.

That is the quiet win of cooking in batches. The chicken, the cheese, and the pasta all get bought in sizes that make sense, cooked once, and stretched across fourteen dinners. You are not paying a restaurant to reheat it for you.
prose.upsell_html: Fourteen dinners, done in one shot, for a price that respects your paycheck. If this is the kind of cooking you want more of, the Thrifty Crew membership is a dollar a month, and it opens up every recipe, every macro breakdown, and every shopping plan we run. Cook once, eat all week, and keep your money where it belongs. In your pocket.

head.description: High protein honey BBQ chicken mac and cheese for meal prep. A blended cottage and cream cheese sauce plus glazed chicken makes 14 bowls at 751 calories and 50.5g protein each.
head.keywords: honey bbq chicken mac and cheese, high protein mac and cheese, meal prep mac and cheese, budget meal prep dinner, cottage cheese pasta sauce, air fryer bbq chicken, high protein dinner, 14 servings meal prep
steps: Toss the diced chicken breast with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Mist with cooking spray and air fry at 350F for 10 to 12 minutes, shaking halfway, or pan-cook over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Toss the hot chicken with the honey and BBQ sauce, then return it to the heat 1 to 2 minutes to caramelize the glaze.
Cook the pasta in salted water to package directions, reserve about a quarter cup of pasta water, then drain and set aside.
Blend the cottage cheese, light cream cheese, shredded cheddar, milk, garlic powder, parsley, black pepper, paprika, salt, and mustard until completely smooth.
Warm the sauce in a saucepan over medium-low for 3 to 5 minutes until thick and glossy, loosening with reserved pasta water as needed.
Fold the drained pasta into the sauce, adding pasta water a little at a time until creamy.
Rest 10 minutes, portion the mac into bowls, top with the honey BBQ chicken, and garnish with parsley.
